name: Earlobe support patches

card.summary: Clear adhesive discs behind the earlobe that support heavy earrings so a stretched piercing looks and feels tidier.
card.note: Support only; they do not repair a torn or split lobe.

quick.overview:
Earlobe support patches are thin clear stickers worn behind the lobe. The earring post goes through them.

They spread an earring's weight so a stretched or thin piercing droops less, which keeps the ear looking neat.
quick.mechanism: The disc adds a wider, firmer base behind the lobe so the post sits higher and straighter in the hole.
quick.risks: They support but do not repair tissue. Badly torn lobes are treated surgically, and adhesives can irritate sensitive skin.

lead: Earlobe support patches are thin, clear adhesive discs worn behind the earlobe, with the earring post passing through them. They spread an earring's weight over a wider area so a stretched or thin piercing droops less, helping people wear statement earrings without a visibly dropped or elongated lobe.

The need comes from how common piercing is. Wikipedia notes the earlobe is pierced more often than any other body location, contains no cartilage and is made of connective tissue, and that heavy earrings often injure it.[1] Reported problems include inflammation, keloids, tearing and splitting of the lobe.[1]
Brand names include Lobe Wonder, Lobe Miracle and Earlift. The patches provide support rather than repair, and no clinical studies of them were found.

chain: Earring weight spread over a wider base
Lobe looks less dropped or stretched
angle.text: The disc adds a wider, firmer base behind the lobe so the earring sits upright. People wear them to keep a stretched or thin piercing looking neat during an event or all day.

infobox: Hours to a few days per patch

paras: Patches are clear, self-adhesive and thin, often with a mesh or criss-cross backing. The post passes through the disc and the earring back then secures it. Reviewers describe wearing them through events lasting many hours, doubling them for heavy earrings, and finding the first push of the post through the patch slightly fiddly.

The earlobe is connective tissue without cartilage, which gives it firmness and elasticity, and it is a common piercing site. Heavy earrings often injure the lobe, and reported complications include inflammation, keloids, tearing and mechanical splitting.[1]

The patches appeal to people who want a statement earring without a visibly dropped lobe. Users also pair them with lighter earrings or flat-back posts. They support the lobe but do not repair a torn or split one, which is addressed in the clinical literature through repair procedures and surgery.
